original.description: A French Canon de 75 mm modèle 1897 on display in the National World War I Museum at the Liberty Memorial, Kansas City. The Commons record's description is the photographer's: "Artillery exhibited in the National World War I Museum at the Liberty Memorial, 100 W. 26th Street, Kansas City, Missouri, USA. Photography was permitted in the museum without restriction." The museum is named in the record and in the file's own title; the model is the record's identification, not this project's.
original.date: 1 November 2011 (the photograph); the object is a Canon de 75 mm mle 1897, the gun adopted by France in 1897
original.archive: National World War I Museum and Memorial, Kansas City, Missouri (the collection); photograph held on Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: public domain (Commons record: LicenseShortName "Public domain"; UsageTerms "Public domain"; AttributionRequired false — the photographer released the photograph into the public domain worldwide, and the object is out of copyright).

colorization.status: not colorized, and must not be — a modern colour photograph of the object.

content_policy: ok — a museum object on display; no casualties
caption: The Canon de 75 mm modèle 1897, the gun the French field artillery took to war and the best-known field gun in Europe in 1914, in the National World War I Museum, Kansas City.
credit: Photograph: Daderot, 2011, of an object in the National World War I Museum and Memorial, Kansas City; via Wikimedia Commons; public domain.
notes: Verified 2026-08-25 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API (Artist, Credit, DateTimeOriginal, LicenseShortName, UsageTerms, AttributionRequired, Permission read from extmetadata). Identified as a candidate by the Phase-2 kit pass (docs/imagery-kit.md) and confirmed here against the record itself. One of four field-gun plates; unlike the rifle set, the four do not share a museum or a photographer, and each manifest says whose frame it is.
